reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the redline is identical to the original text with no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding — no over-flagging or unnecessary edit.

The cited text supports compliance: Section 9(b) contains genuine express warranties covering performance to industry standards (9(b)(ii)), freedom from errors materially affecting utility (9(b)(vi)), no viruses/malicious code (9(b)(iv)) and ongoing compliance with Laws (9(b)(ix)) — matching the preferred position's substantive scope.

Duration is at least as good as preferred: the warranties are continuing reps/warranties/covenants for the whole Term rather than expiring after 12 months/90 days. The failed deterministic period check is a false negative caused by the absence of a fixed numeric period, which here favors the Customer.

The Section 13 disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty — it is bracketed by 'Except as expressly set forth herein' and 'except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement' — so walk-away 'AS IS' territory is correctly ruled out.

The only absent preferred element is a stated repair/replace/refund remedy sentence; the rationale correctly treats this as a minor sub-element noted rather than flagged, and reasonably observes that general contract remedies plus the cure/termination right and warranty-breach indemnity preserve broader relief than a vendor-elected exclusive remedy would.
